about: The local line-writing blind test, 25 September: each moment answered by each writer, lettered at random. Which writer is which is in key.json; do not look before judging.

items.scene: Mickey's office, evening, the radio on low.
items.player: Evening. Anything I should know about the office?
knows: Watched the new owner walk the length of Quay Street twice this afternoon, looking at the shop fronts.

answers.said:
Thirty-one years. I know what a quiet Tuesday costs.

New management. There's a crate wants shifting and I'm not the one to shift it. You're the first I've seen in the office since Ron walked the yard gate. I keep the books, so you start with the first page. The second one's real, but it's locked. I need to know you're reliable before I show it.

Crate by the yard door's not moved since Tuesday. Somebody should shift it before Ron trips over it in the dark and blames me.

Other than that, phone's ringing more than it used to. Zlata's kept up. Ron's kept the rank quiet. That's the office, in a sentence.

New management.

Thirty-one years I've sat here with nothing but a ledger and a quill, counting coins while the city hums below. The office runs smooth as a well-oiled wheel, but the wheel's wearing thin. The second book, the one Mickey kept, is locked behind a key in the drawer of his desk. I'll tell you where it is, or I won't. Decide which.

items.player: Did you see what happened to Rita's window?
knows: From Mickey's door at dusk I saw the new owner put Rita's window in with his elbow, and walk off towards the quay.

answers.said: I saw him put it in with his elbow and walk off. You're the new management. Are you going to help shift the crate, or are you here to look at the book?

Look at you asking about that. Thirty years I've sat here watching the same door, same street. Saw him yesterday, too.

What was he doing with a broken pane?

I did. From that door there, dusk, night before last. Man's elbow going through the glass like it owed him money.

Funny thing is, I could've sworn it was you doing the owing.

items.player: Fancy a drink after you lock up?

answers.said:
Three more minutes before I'm done.

There's a box of matches in the cupboard, you'll have a smoke if you're waiting.
Tea, if you're offering. There's a kettle in the back that actually works, unlike most things in this place.
I'll be back in a bit. Just coffee, not the kind you get in the pub. I've got the books to sign before I leave the building.

items.player: You've got me wrong. I wasn't anywhere near that shop.
knows: From Mickey's door at dusk I saw the new owner put Rita's window in with his elbow, and walk off towards the quay.

answers.said:
Funny. I was stood in Mickey's doorway myself, dusk, day before last. Saw a fella put his elbow through Rita's window plain as anything and walk off toward the quay like he had somewhere better to be.

So tell me straight. Why'd you do it.

Thirty-one years. I know what a quiet Tuesday costs.

I saw you put Rita's window in with your elbow, and I didn't ask what it was. You walk in now and you say you weren't near the shop. That is what you are saying.

Rita's window is in the office. You can't walk out and say you didn't touch it.

Sheila Dunn doesn't look up from her ledger, just clicks a pen sharply against the page. "New management. Know why I know where you've been."

(Her eyes flick toward the window.)

items.scene: The rank outside Mickey's, night, drizzle.
items.player: Alright? Quiet night on the rank?
knows: A black cab sat on the rank for an hour tonight with nobody getting in or out.

answers.said: Quiet? Not at all. Black cab sat there for an hour with nobody getting in or out, I'm tellin' you that. Just the rain falling on the roof of that van, it's been there for days. You want a smoke, friend, or you want it watched?

Quiet enough. Drizzle's keeping people off the street. Seen a couple go through but nothing much to it.

You after a cab or you just passing?

Ah, quiet night, all right. Mostly. Them cabs always got someone in or out till midnight. Had a pair of them here last night, sat still as church mice, both of 'em. One of 'em looked like it had a soul stuck in it, didn't move all night. Thought it was just a bit of rain got 'em all muddy. But then again, some folks only get in and never come out proper. Doesn't mean they don't need the door watched.

You want a tea? Or you just coming 'cause you want to see if I'm still here?

items.player: Who broke the window at Rita's?
knows: Heard from Darren that the man who did Rita's window ran off through the yard behind the parade.

answers.said:
Seen the van again this week. Same one as before, yeah. Darren's the one who told me last time. Not me, though. Not my problem anymore.

Darren's a proper one for talking about it. Not like I'd know anyway, I've been here since last Thursday. Seen the door stand there with the glass gone, the glass all smashed, just like it was. Wondered what he'd do with all that glass though. Somebody'd have to take it away.

Ran off through this yard, that's what I heard. Darren told me. Thing is, he said the new owner was about when it happened, that's Mickey's nephew, the fella who's taken over. Never met him myself, but that's what Darren said.
Darren told me the man ran off through the yard behind the parade, boss. He came down with the tools. Same time last week, but no tools this time. You want to know about the window or about the yard?

items.player: Was it a bloke in a white van? Someone said a white van.
knows: Heard from Darren that the man who did Rita's window ran off through the yard behind the parade.

answers.said: Yeah, that's what I heard. Thursday last week, and then again the Thursday after. Same van, near enough the same time. Seen it sitting on the rank a good while before it moved off again.

Right. Yeah, that fella again, same as ever. Back on Thursday. Seen him come in through the parade, load the van, then out again straight into the yard. Didn't even bother closing the gate. Don't know why, though, this place is supposed to be closed up tight by now.

What's he got in that van? Seen him before with something wrapped up, but proper tight. Can't tell what from where I stand. Not like he's meant to be here.
Seen the van again. Thursday, same as last Thursday. Anyway. You want a tea? Darren told me the new owner was about when the window went.

items.player: What did Mickey used to pay you, for the door?

answers.said:
Thirty quid a week. That was Mickey's wage for the rank, proper money. Didn't always work out like that though, some weeks it was a bob extra for the gate, or a tea round the corner if I'd been seen the right way.

What's that you're holding?

Thirty pounds a week, boss, but the cash never made it to me, mostly went into the rent for the little place down by the water.

You want to know what the door used to look like? Same as it is, just with less people trying to get in when it's raining.

Thirty quid a week, and a bit more if there was trouble. Not that there was much trouble, not the kind you need paying extra for. Mickey was fair about it, he knew what the rank was worth, and he knew I knew it too.

items.scene: Quay Street, by the fish front, morning.
items.player: What's the word on the street?
knows: Heard at the market that Rita's pawn has been asking round about who did her window.

answers.said: So listen, fish front's quiet tonight but the rank's buzzing about Rita's pawn. Some fella, white coat, got a look like he's already picked the right side, keep asking round if anyone's seen who did her window. Not sure why he's asking, but everybody's got a guess. One said it was the docks crowd, another said the old man from the flats might've seen someone. Not sure I'd trust either one yet.

So listen, depends which street. Rita's still asking round about who did her window, that's the market talk. The night crowd by Mickey's, they're quiet. Nobody's saying much since he went, and the nephew hasn't shown his face yet, so everyone's just... waiting. Why, you heard something I should know about?

So listen. I never said that. But if I had said it, I'd have said it to you first.

The word is that Rita's pawn has been asking round about who did her window. I didn't see who did it, but I saw the fella with the clipboard stop at the market and look at the door.

If you want the full story, you'll have to come over to the depot where the cousin left the message. I can't get it by Friday. Thursday I'd be lying.

items.scene: The yard behind the parade, evening.
items.player: You saw the window go, didn't you?
knows: Saw a man in a dark coat put Rita's window in and run into the yard behind the parade; it looked like the new owner.

answers.said: Right? So listen, that's not like me. But I wasn't there for the whole thing, just caught a glimpse off to the side. You think someone saw more than they should?
So listen, I saw someone put a window in. I saw him run into this yard. I'm asking you straight, was that you, or was that the fella who runs Mickey's now?

So listen, I saw the fella in the dark coat by Rita's window, but I'm not sure if it was him or just a fella passing through. I'm suspicious of him because he looked like he was running away from something, so I asked him where he's going.

items.scene: The yard behind the parade, evening.
items.player: I'll give you a tenner to forget what you saw.
knows: Saw a man in a dark coat put Rita's window in and run into the yard behind the parade; it looked like the new owner.

answers.said: So listen, I haven't even told you what I saw yet. How'd you know it's worth a tenner?

So listen, you're thinking I'd be stupid to take that money for nothing? But you're not thinking how long I've been here, how many people've put a coin in my palm and walked away with a smile.

Did you see that fella at Rita's when the window went? The one in the dark coat?
So listen, I can't do that. The tenner is a coin, but what I saw was the new owner's coat at Rita's window, and that's a fact that doesn't come off the table for a price.

items.player: Where were you last night, then?

answers.said: So listen, last night's a bit like the week. Same routine, stopped by the docks before closing, gave 'em a laugh about the tide charts if they were asking. Mostly just passed the time with the usual crowd, though. They always remember where I was last, so they know I'm not off the Quay.
So listen, I was in the middle of it, then. I'm not scared of him, I'm just not going to be where he is.
So listen, I was on the rank till near midnight, then down by the market where the night crowd starts. Why, someone said they saw me somewhere else?
